title: Step from a tape write action
statement: Let $M$ be a $k$-tape Turing machine and $c$ a configuration. Suppose $c$ has state $q$, and the transition of $M$ at $q$ on the symbols currently read is the action that moves the input head by $\mathrm{inp}$, writes $s$ on the scanned cell of tape $i$, moves that tape's head by $m$, makes no other writes or output, and enters state $q'$. Then the next configuration has state $q'$, input-head position obtained by moving $c$'s input head by $\mathrm{inp}$ with boundary clamping, tape $i$'s scanned cell set to $s$, and tape $i$'s head position increased by $m$; all other components are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $s$ is an optional symbol, with absence representing a blank
the transition at $q$ on the currently read symbols is the specified tape action
